quest.title: A Gifted Rose: Prickly as Thorns
quest.description: The old man who lives alone on the outskirts of the village may be the flower grower mentioned by Sabbah. Help him clean up his nursery.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x4, Delicious Shawarma Wrap x2, Delicious Tahchin x2, Glabrous Beans x2

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: What are you kids doing? Come to laugh at this old man "growing rocks," have you?

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: I'm fine! I don't need the other villagers to worry about me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, no need to be so hostile from the get-go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're mistaken. We're not from Aaru Village, and we're not here to laugh at you.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Passers-by? Uh...

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Normally, only some old friends of mine would come over to tell me to give up on the nursery and move back to the village.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: And a few bad kids too. They keep coming over here to cause trouble.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: It's my first time seeing children dressed up like this. What is it that you do?

choices.text: I'm a traveler looking for my family.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, we've traveled a long way for this, and gone through many adventures together.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}'s a righteous soul through and through.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We don't do things like bullying lonely old folks.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So there's no need to worry, gramps. We're not bad guys.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Ahem. How embarrassing, to have to apologize to two children. But I am sorry. I shouldn't have made assumptions.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Children, please accept my — Affan's — most sincere apologies.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: You children are very capable to be supporting yourselves at such a young age. Quite impressive. Much better than me at your age.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: So based on what you just said, I can request your help when I have a problem that I can't solve, yes?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? Do you mean you have a commission for us?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's the problem?

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I originally had two nurseries. One is here, and the other is to the west of the village.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I've gotten quite old, so it's getting harder for me to tend to both places. I didn't check on the other nursery for just a few days, and it was destroyed by some strange black stuff.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: It's terribly dangerous. Once I went in, I thought I wouldn't be able to come back out. I know better than to try to go in there again.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: My greatest hope now is to restore that nursery so that I can grow flowers there again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #It doesn't sound too complicated. What do you think? Should we accept this commission, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: The nursery is to the west of the village. Don't get lost!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No problem! Don't worry about it.

choices.text: I'm an adventurer exploring the world.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! We've climbed many, many mountains, and crossed lakes and seas to get to Sumeru.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you call it? Uh, we're... big-hearted adventurers.

choices.text: I heard that someone's growing flowers here.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Yeah, I'm growing flowers, not some dumb rocks.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: I thought... Ugh. Never mind, what am I even supposed to say now...

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: You two are back? How is the nursery? Do you think it can be saved?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've taken care of it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain the Withering to Affan.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: I see. So that's why. I knew something was off when so much black stuff just appeared out of the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Good, good. Now I can finally plant some seeds without worries.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: When these three seeds sprout, bloom and produce seeds again, I'll plant them in the ground there. Then the land will be covered with these flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? These strangely-shaped rocks...? Can flowers grow out of them?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where did you buy these from, Grandpa Affan? Did you get scammed or something?

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: You have good hearts. But don't worry, children. Mora can't buy these flower seeds.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: The old... I mean, a friend of mine gave me these three precious seeds. So of course they are different from normal seedlings.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The more Paimon hears about it, the weirder it sounds. Grandpa Affan, just what are you growing?

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Hehe, what I'm planting is a friend's wish.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a strange answer. Can you really plant that sort of thing?

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Child, you wouldn't understand even if I told you. Come visit me again when you get the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: This field might look empty now, but these three seeds will one day sprout and bloom in this nursery.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: There will be more and more of them in the future. Haha, and they will surely create a beautiful scene.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Alright, alright. Since I asked for your help, I will be sure to compensate you.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Take this, children. I can't give you much, so this is all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, commission complete! Paimon's a little hungry after all that running around.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I was the one running though...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon was providing running commentary. That takes energy too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't sweat the small stuff! How about we use our payment to buy ourselves a treat, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's see how much we got and how many meals we can buy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, most of the stuff here is food instead of Mora... Shawarma, Tahchin, and lots of vegetables.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is way too much. Did we take a whole day's rations away from Grandpa Affan?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But he lives alone outside the village. It can't be easy for him, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Never mind the Mora. If he gave us all his rations, then... It just feels wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And he was planting seeds that looked like stones, saying that he was planting... a wish?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it possible that he's been living on his own for so long that he's started to imagine things?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is worrying. Let's pay him a visit when we can find the time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, commission complete! Paimon's a little hungry after all that running around.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I was the one running though...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon was providing running commentary. That takes energy too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't sweat the small stuff! How about we use our payment to buy ourselves a treat, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's see how much we got and how many meals we can buy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, most of the stuff here is food instead of Mora... Shawarma, Tahchin, and lots of vegetables.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But he lives alone outside the village. It can't be easy for him, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Never mind the Mora. If he gave us all his rations, then... It just feels wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And he was planting seeds that looked like stones, saying that he was planting... a wish?

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: Ah, I haven't had time to cook yet, so I'm afraid I have nothing with which to receive you as guests.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: So, this other kid is your friend, huh? She's pretty cute.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Do you want to come see the flowers when they bloom?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No problem.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: They will most likely bloom in a few days. Come back later to see the flowers you helped to plant.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay.

response.speaker: Affan
response.text: Alright, I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Which Darshan were you with, by the way?

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Oh, I could talk for three whole days about that!

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I was with Amurta and specialized in plant evolution, so you could say my work was evidence-based.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: That means it is impossible to reach new conclusions without new forms of evidence. Simply put, fossils are necessary for the study of historical plants.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: But there are only so many fossil samples available, and the Akademiya is limited in its ability to provide new ones.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Those were the circumstances, yet the institute still demanded results.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: So some people would just take a previous study, revise or add something to it, and turn it in. You also find that quite pointless, right?

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: In truth, we could make new discoveries for sure if we looked towards history and geography for new materials.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Certain literary documents that Amurta would usually ignore could be used as well, though that would surely cross into Vahumana and Haravatat territory.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I was not proficient in those fields, and requesting the related files was too troublesome, never mind working with their researchers...

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: But I believe that if we could actually work together as a team, many questions of the past would finally be answered.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: It's a shame that we couldn't continue our collaboration attempts. I must say that people in Vahumana and Haravatat have very peculiar perspectives, though...

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I had to be very careful with my wording and phrasing in my submissions to them to avoid misunderstandings and misinterpretations.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Before I was kicked out of the Akademiya, I was still in the middle of an argument with someone from Haravatat. Now I can't even do that...

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Ah, I just rambled for a long time... But it feels good.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Before you got here, I really didn't have many friends, and it could get pretty lonely.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Very few people in the village are into gardening.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: ...Well, that's not entirely true. An old man living to the north of the village also plowed a plot to grow flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I've visited him before. He's a slightly eccentric old man.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I saw him planting stones, but he insisted that they were flowers, and even kicked me out.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: It must be lonely, living all by himself. I can understand that.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: You helped me with my Sumeru Roses... Maybe you can help him with his plants too.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: You and Paimon should visit him if you get a chance.

dialogues.speaker: Affan
dialogues.text: The nursery is to the west of the village. Give it a try, and see if you can save it.
